findings.observed: The stem asks which conclusion supports cells being independently living units; the sole keyed correct answer says 'It depends on the host’s metabolic and translational machinery', which describes a virus rather than cellular independence.
findings.risk: An HL student may be rewarded for a response that contradicts the question's stated subject.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the selection item a21-p1a-2 in the lesson's questions array; in a local QA browser use HL mode, navigate to the practice route and identify its stem and keyed feedback.
findings.recommendation: A qualified IB Biology reviewer should correct or clarify the stem, options and feedback as a complete item; do not flip the boolean key without reviewing the item.
findings.confirmedBehavior: In real Chromium the host-dependent keyed choice is displayed for a stem about independently living cells and the app marks that selection correct.

findings.observed: Across multiple topics, all wrong choices of many MCQs share identical explanation text. The correct option is still structurally unique. A source-data inspection flagged hundreds of cases; the new static audit lists each exact ID when run.
findings.risk: Students may be told the correct concept without learning why their particular misconception is incorrect.
findings.reproduction: Review any listed item and compare feedback values for all incorrect options. In the browser, choose two different incorrect answers after using Try again.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize high-frequency and conceptually difficult questions for distinct, diagnostic distractor explanations; retain correct science and original item IDs.
findings.confirmedBehavior: Wrong option IDs 2 and 3 of a21-p1a-1 were separately submitted in Chromium and received identical feedback. 420 medium static findings remain editorial review candidates.

findings.observed: readStudy and saveStudy use a module-scoped in-memory Map. The lesson UI explicitly states that answers persist across routes in the same tab but that refresh starts a new session. Written drafts use this same transient state.
findings.risk: Students can lose unsaved answers, response drafts or flashcard position on page refresh, close or tab crash, even though route navigation preserves them.
findings.reproduction: In a disposable local browser, enter a written response or attempt MCQ, navigate away and back to check in-tab retention, then refresh to confirm loss.
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly whether this is intended ephemeral practice. If longer persistence is desired, propose opt-in local storage or authenticated persistence with privacy review; do not modify shared progress implementation on QA branch.
findings.confirmedBehavior: A written response persisted after route changes within the current tab and disappeared after browser refresh; self-review marking guidance was shown.

validatedNoIssue.note: Case-insensitive duplicate detection produced a false positive: options intentionally differ in capitalization to test binomial nomenclature. The new detector preserves case and does not flag this.
